assumption: One normal human red blood cell has a mean diameter of about 7.5 μm, expressed as 0.0000075 m.
sourceNote: NIH's NCBI Bookshelf says normal human red blood cells have a mean diameter of about 7.5 μm; conversion to metres is exact.

assumption: One FIFA-recommended field of play is 105 m long.
sourceNote: FIFA Stadium Guidelines specify recommended field dimensions of 105 m by 68 m.

assumption: Earth's equatorial diameter is 12,756 km, expressed as 12,756,000 m.
sourceNote: NASA gives Earth's equatorial diameter as 12,756 km; conversion to metres is exact.

assumption: One Lifetime six-foot folding table is 72 in long, expressed as exactly 1.8288 m.
sourceNote: Lifetime specifies a 72 in by 30 in six-foot folding table; inch-to-metre conversion is exact.

assumption: Using NASA's 2018 infographic configuration: the International Space Station had an approximate mass of 420,000 kg.
sourceNote: NASA infographic lists ISS mass as 420,000 kg.

assumption: One iPhone 17 weighs 177 g, expressed here as 0.177 kg.
sourceNote: Apple technical specifications list iPhone 17 weight as 177 g; g-to-kg conversion is exact.

assumption: One Earth has a mass of 5.97219 × 10²⁴ kg.
sourceNote: NASA's Earth and Moon comparison lists Earth's mass as 5,972,190,000,000,000,000,000,000 kg.

assumption: One 0.177 kg iPhone 17 lifted 1 m requires 0.177 kg × 9.80665 m/s² × 1 m = 1.73577705 J.
sourceNote: Apple gives iPhone 17 mass as 177 g; NIST standard gravity is 9.80665 m/s² at https://www.nist.gov/pml/special-publication-811/nist-guide-si-appendix-b-conversion-factors/nist-guide-si-appendix-b8.

referenceLabel: Apple 70-watt adapters running for a minute
assumption: One Apple 70 W USB-C adapter delivering its rated power for exactly 60 s supplies 70 J/s × 60 s = 4,200 J.
sourceNote: Apple identifies the adapter as 70 W; energy is exact arithmetic using NIST's W = J/s definition and a defined 60 s duration.

referenceLabel: Hoover Dam powerplants running at nameplate capacity for an hour
assumption: One Hoover powerplant operating at its 2,080 MW nameplate capacity for one hour produces 2.08 × 10⁹ J/s × 3,600 s = 7.488 × 10¹² J.
sourceNote: The U.S. Bureau of Reclamation gives Hoover's nameplate capacity as about 2,080 MW; the one-hour duration and W = J/s arithmetic are explicit reference conditions.

assumption: One 105 m by 68 m FIFA-recommended pitch has area 7,140 m².
sourceNote: FIFA supplies 105 m and 68 m dimensions; area is exact multiplication.

assumption: One 28 m by 15 m FIBA court has area 420 m².
sourceNote: FIBA Official Basketball Rules specify 28 m by 15 m; area is exact multiplication.

assumption: Earth's surface area is 510,064,472 km², expressed as 510,064,472,000,000 m².
sourceNote: NASA lists Earth's surface area as 510,064,472 km²; square-kilometre-to-square-metre conversion is exact.

assumption: Brunei Darussalam has land area 5,765 km², expressed as 5,765,000,000 m².
sourceNote: Brunei's government Information Department gives its total land area as 5,765 km²; square-kilometre-to-square-metre conversion is exact.

assumption: One single-layer Blu-ray Disc holds 25 GB.
sourceNote: Blu-ray Disc Association states single-layer discs are 25 GB.

assumption: One LTO-9 data tape has 18 TB native capacity, expressed as 18,000 GB.
sourceNote: Fujifilm specifies 18 TB native capacity per LTO-9 cartridge; decimal TB-to-GB conversion is exact.

assumption: One 256 GB iPhone 17 configuration has 256 GB of storage capacity.
sourceNote: Apple technical specifications list a 256 GB iPhone 17 capacity option.

assumption: One regulation football half lasts 45 min = 2,700 s before added time.
sourceNote: IFAB Law 7 specifies two equal 45-minute halves; minute-to-second conversion is exact.

assumption: One ISS orbit takes about 90 min, expressed as 5,400 s.
sourceNote: NASA says the ISS orbits Earth once every 90 minutes; minute-to-second conversion is exact.

assumption: One Earth rotation with respect to the Sun takes 24 h, expressed as 86,400 s.
sourceNote: NASA Glenn says Earth completes one revolution every 24 hours with respect to the Sun; hour-to-second conversion is exact.

assumption: The twentieth century ran from 1901 through 2000 and contained 36,525 Gregorian days, or 3,155,760,000 s.
sourceNote: U.S. Naval Observatory identifies the twentieth century as 1901–2000; its Gregorian leap-year rules at https://aa.usno.navy.mil/faq/leap_years yield 25 leap days, so 100 × 365 + 25 = 36,525 days.

referenceLabel: Hoover Dam powerplants at nameplate capacity
assumption: One Hoover Dam powerplant has about 2,080 MW nameplate capacity, expressed as 2,080,000,000 W.
sourceNote: The U.S. Bureau of Reclamation gives Hoover's nameplate capacity as about 2,080 MW; conversion to watts is exact.

assumption: One Apple USB-C power adapter is rated at 70 W.
sourceNote: Apple product page identifies this adapter as 70 W.

assumption: One explicitly defined 10 W LED bulb draws 10 W while lit.
sourceNote: The 10 W lamp is a defined reference condition; NIST defines watt as the unit of power.

assumption: One standard atmosphere is 101,325 Pa.
sourceNote: NIST pressure table gives 1 atm = 101,325 Pa.

referenceLabel: the pressure of a nine-bar espresso extraction
assumption: One espresso extraction at Breville's stated 9 bar pressure is 900,000 Pa.
sourceNote: Breville states espresso extraction uses 9 bar; 1 bar = 100,000 Pa from NIST's pressure table at https://www.nist.gov/pml/owm/metric-si/unit-conversion/pressure-and-gas-flow-unit-conversions.

referenceLabel: the gauge pressure of a tyre set to 35 psi
assumption: One car tyre explicitly set to 35 psi has pressure 35 × 6,894.757 Pa = 241,316.495 Pa.
sourceNote: NIST gives 1 psi = 6,894.757 Pa; the 35 psi tyre setting is an explicit familiar reference condition, not a claim about every vehicle.

referenceLabel: the International Space Station orbital speed
assumption: The ISS travels about 28,000 km/h, which is about 7,777.777778 m/s.
sourceNote: NASA gives about 28,000 km/h; conversion to m/s divides by 3.6, retaining NASA's approximate character.

referenceLabel: Usain Bolt’s average world-record sprint speed
assumption: Bolt's 100 m record completed in 9.58 s has average speed 100 m ÷ 9.58 s = 10.438413361 m/s.
sourceNote: World Athletics lists Bolt's 100 m world record as 9.58 s; average speed is direct arithmetic from the event distance and time.

referenceLabel: the speed of light in vacuum
assumption: One light beam in vacuum travels at exactly 299,792,458 m/s.
sourceNote: NIST SI material describes the metre through the fixed speed of light in vacuum; 299,792,458 m/s is exact by definition.

assumption: One F-1 engine produced 1.5 million lbf, converted as 1,500,000 × 4.4482216152605 N = 6,672,332.423 N.
sourceNote: NASA gives 1.5 million pounds of thrust per F-1 engine; NIST gives 1 lbf = 4.4482216152605 N at standard gravity: https://www.nist.gov/pml/special-publication-811/nist-guide-si-footnotes.

referenceLabel: iPhone 17 weights on a standard-gravity force plate
assumption: One 0.177 kg iPhone 17 at standard gravity weighs 0.177 kg × 9.80665 m/s² = 1.73577705 N.
sourceNote: Apple gives 177 g for iPhone 17; NIST gives standard gravity 9.80665 m/s² at https://www.nist.gov/pml/special-publication-811/nist-guide-si-appendix-b-conversion-factors/nist-guide-si-appendix-b8; calculation is direct multiplication.

referenceLabel: International Space Stations on a standard-gravity force plate
assumption: An imagined weight under standard Earth gravity using the approximately 420,000 kg ISS mass in NASA's 2018 infographic; not the station's orbital weight.
sourceNote: NASA's 2018 infographic lists ISS mass as 420,000 kg; NIST standard gravity is 9.80665 m/s² at https://www.nist.gov/pml/special-publication-811/nist-guide-si-appendix-b-conversion-factors/nist-guide-si-appendix-b8.

assumption: Approximately 1.98 × 10²⁰ N, using the masses and Earth–Moon separation in NASA's worked gravitational-force example.
sourceNote: NASA's PUMAS worked example tabulates the Earth-Moon gravitational interaction as 1.98E+20 N from its stated masses, separation, and gravitational constant.

assumption: Australia's National Electricity Market operates around 50 Hz.
sourceNote: AEMO states Australia's NEM operates within a frequency range around 50 Hz.

assumption: The defining caesium-133 transition frequency is 9,192,631,770 Hz.
sourceNote: BIPM working document states 9,192,631,770 cycles of the caesium resonance for one second.

assumption: One concert-A tuning fork vibrates at 440 Hz.
sourceNote: Yamaha's tuning guide identifies an A tuning fork as 440 Hz.

assumption: Using NASA's 2018 infographic configuration: the International Space Station had approximately 388 m³ of habitable volume.
sourceNote: NASA infographic lists ISS habitable volume as 388 m³.

referenceLabel: FIFA football pitches under one millimetre of rain
assumption: One 105 m by 68 m FIFA pitch covered by a defined 1 mm layer of rain holds 105 m × 68 m × 0.001 m = 7.14 m³.
sourceNote: FIFA supplies the 105 m by 68 m pitch dimensions; the 1 mm rain layer is an explicit bounded scene and volume is direct arithmetic.

assumption: One Lake Superior has volume 12,100 km³, expressed as 12,100,000,000,000 m³.
sourceNote: NOAA lists Lake Superior's volume as 12,100 km³; cubic-kilometre-to-cubic-metre conversion is exact.

referenceLabel: fresh water at its freezing point
assumption: Fresh water's freezing point is 0 °C under the conventional Celsius reference.
sourceNote: NIST states water freezes at 0 °C on the Celsius scale.

assumption: Water's boiling point is about 100 °C on the Celsius scale at standard atmospheric pressure.
sourceNote: NIST states water boils at about 100 °C; its source context is the conventional Celsius scale.

referenceLabel: liquid nitrogen at its boiling point
assumption: Liquid nitrogen boils at approximately −196 °C at standard atmospheric pressure (1 atm).
sourceNote: Air Products Safetygram 7 lists the boiling point at 1 atm as −195.8 °C, rounded here to −196 °C.
